rubrics.justification: Describes an expanded blastocyst with thinned zona, visible ICM, and cohesive TE consistent with the reported 3AA, while appropriately noting limits of a single static image. Slight imprecision around stage terminology keeps it from being fully precise.

Thoroughly integrates age, male-factor diagnosis, endometrial thickness, BMI, ovarian reserve markers, oocyte maturity, prior cycle history, and sperm parameters with embryo quality to frame prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent: favorable morphology plus young age and good uterine factors support a good prognosis, while uncertainty from untested ploidy and transfer/receptivity factors appropriately tempers estimates.

Recommendations are well aligned with standard IVF practice, especially elective single embryo transfer in a 29-year-old with a good-quality day-5 blastocyst and cautious use of PGT-A. Minor looseness in describing Gardner stage 3 as expanded rather than full blastocyst prevents a perfect score.

Provides clear practical recommendations for proceeding with single embryo transfer, standard luteal support, post-transfer activity, and reasonable next steps if unsuccessful. Useful and nuanced, though not highly protocol-specific.
